paintings.title: Poplar in Winter
paintings.description: On a sketching trip around Wetherby, Yorkshire, I noticed this singular grouping of trees. Whilst all the other trees had lost their leaves, the poplar was hanging on to make the most of the daylight.

paintings.title: Byland Abbey - Sunset
paintings.description: Byland Abbey is often overlooked next to its more famous neighbour at Rievaulx but it is a beautiful and tranquil place, especially as the sun sets. This view is taken from the far side of the monastic fishponds, near the village of Wass

paintings.title: Alnwick Castle
paintings.description: The beautiful castle at Alnwick, seen from across the fields

paintings.title: Derwentwater
paintings.description: This piece was painted plein air as a Wildcard for the 2025 series of Landscape Artist of the Year.

paintings.title: Troller's Ghyll
paintings.description: Trollers Ghyll is a collapsed cavern in limestone country. It is a place of legend and is home to the Bargest - a huge, black dog with red saucer-sized eyes! This beast hunts down lost travellers to devour them and was the inspiration for The Hound of the Baskervilles by Conan Doyle.

paintings.title: The Boggle Holes - Runswick Bay
paintings.description: The Boggle Holes were originally thought to have been created by trolls (or boggles) as places to live. Local children were no doubt kept in line with a threat of the boggles! In actual fact they were created by miners looking for jet

paintings.title: Timble Ings - Sunrise
paintings.description: This image is from the local woods of Timble Ings, in North Yorkshire. This area was once heavily forested but storms have decimated the trees and allow light to stream through. I was captured by the cloud formation and the gaunt, solitary trees, silhouetted against the brilliant sky.

paintings.title: The Sandbeds, Otley
paintings.description: The Sandbeds lie south of Otley, where the river Wharfe slows and creates wonderful reflections of the riverside trees and shrubs.

paintings.title: The Conifer Forest
paintings.description: Oil painting inspired by the Russian 19th century painter Ivan Shishkin. Shishkin was a wonderful painter of the forests in Russia and I often carry his work around in my head. The layout of the trees in this work is actually based on a conifer plantation north of Otley, West Yorkshire, whilst the idea of the stream is from one of Shishkin's works. An amalgamation of the past and the present.

paintings.title: Stag Rocks from Bamburgh Castle
paintings.description: A summer's view from Bamburgh castle, across the dunes to Stag Rocks and, in the distance, Holy Island under a shower of rain

paintings.title: Last of the Snow
paintings.description: An early morning view of Timble Woods, Otley, with the last of the snow cloaking the ground.

paintings.title: Pockstones Moor
paintings.description: This beautiful moorland lies in the grounds of the Bolton Abbey estate. The tracks stretch for miles across open moorland and one can walk for miles with just the curlews and skylarks for company.

paintings.title: Beech Tree by the Wharfe
paintings.description: One of a group of tree studies - this beech tree stands by the River Wharfe just outside Otley and is, in fact, two trees growing together. The remarkable sinuous nature of the trunks and roots are rather beautiful and grotesque.

paintings.title: Runswick Bay
paintings.description: This bay is a beautiful and quiet respite from the hustle and bustle of Whitby. On a summer's day it sparkles.

paintings.title: Harnessing the Storm
paintings.description: This is an actual storm I witnessed looking towards the wind turbines near Harrogate. I was enthralled by the changes of scale - the wind turbines are enormous when viewed close-up but are dwarfed by nature in all its majesty.

paintings.title: Fountains Abbey
paintings.description: The iconic and much painted ruins of Fountains Abbey, seen from a slightly different angle to the usual

paintings.title: Frost Morning
paintings.description: This scene was captured in the fields above my hometown of Otley. The town itself was shrouded in freezing fog but as I drove onto higher ground, the mist lifted and I was suddenly in beautiful, winter light.

paintings.title: Sunrise at Thruscross Reservoir
paintings.description: A beautiful backlit set of pines caught my attention on this cold but gorgeous morning at Thruscross Reservoir

paintings.title: East Lagoon at Staveley
paintings.description: Staveley Nature Reserve lies near Harrogate, Yorkshire. Originally a gravel quarry, this is now a peaceful wildlife sanctuary. Here is the east lagoon on a summer's day.

paintings.title: Beech Trees at Thruscross
paintings.description: Another of my tree studies - this time of a row of beech trees on the River Washburn, at Thruscross

paintings.title: The Gathering  Storm - Wharfedale
paintings.description: This view was taken at the end of a long day dry-stone walling on the moors above Bolton Priory in Wharfedale, Yorkshire. The clouds loomed over me and I felt miniscule in the landscape.

paintings.title: Still Winter's Morning
paintings.description: This view is from the nature reserve at Fairburn Ings. Once home to the largest slag heap in Europe (what a boast!) it has been transformed into a thriving and beautiful place by the RSPB. This area of the reserve is home to burgeoning silver birch and alder, thriving in the damp conditions.

paintings.title: Lindisfarne - First Light
paintings.description: The iconic Lindisfarne castle bathed in the glow of a sunrise.

paintings.title: Hanging Wood Lane, Thruscross
paintings.description: Hanging Wood lane leads to the reservoir at Thruscross in the beautiful Washburn Valley, Yorkshire. The hillside to the left was heavily planted with conifers for commercial forestry. They were removed a year ago and left this pair of silver birches. Their shape was eye-catching as they had grown up in the shade of the light-hungry conifers and so their branches had stretched away and into the light over the lane.

paintings.title: Respite - Storm Eunice from Snowden Crags
paintings.description: In early 2022, the UK was battered by a series of storms - it is estimated that some 8 million trees were destroyed. During storm Eunice, I ventured onto the moors and sketched this scene from my car during a lull - I raced back to begin the process of committing the scene to canvas.

paintings.title: Covey Hall Farm
paintings.description: This isolated farm lies on high ground near to my hometown of Otley, Yorkshire. On this particular day, the mist was heavy and tenacious, turning buildings into mere shapes, and turning the weather-battered hawthorn into strange forms.

paintings.title: Saltburn Beach in Winter
paintings.description: Another in the popular series of Saltburn paintings, this time showing the beach in winter.

paintings.title: Woodland Clearing
paintings.description: A gentle summer's day on the Farnley Estate, near Otley

paintings.title: Early  Morning Rain, Timble
paintings.description: Timble is a wonderfully inspirational place for me - an area of mixed deciduous and conifer trees, with open moorland. It is very popular but if you leave the beaten track you can find quiet, reflective pools. This scene was early one morning as a gentle rain disturbed the surface of the water.

paintings.title: Evening Light at Marske
paintings.description: This is from a photograph that I took almost three years ago one evening whilst strolling up the beach to Marske, on the Yorkshire coast. The sky was stunning.

paintings.title: The Clearing
paintings.description: Original oil painting 65x50cm on canvas. The cool of the pine forest is depicted here, contrasting with the heat of the clearing. Painted at Timble Woods near Otley.

paintings.title: Spring Light
paintings.description: This scene, from the nature reserve at Staveley, near Harrogate, depicts that beautiful early spring light.

paintings.title: Harvest - East Park at Farnley
paintings.description: The summer of 2022 was one of the hottest in the UK, with temperatures reaching 40 degrees Celsius. This scene is just up the road from where I live, in one of the fields that belong to the Farnley estate, where JMW Turner spent many of his summers.

paintings.title: Woodland Track - Timble
paintings.description: Conifer plantations make for wonderful studies due to their density and their deep greens and shadows. Here is one such study from Timble forest near my home town of Otley.

paintings.title: Winter Sunrise at Staveley
paintings.description: The nature reserve at Staveley is a major source of inspiration, offering clear, flat views and large skies. Here the winter light is just rising by one of the many pools that fringe the reserve.

paintings.title: Ripon Minster from Studley Royal
paintings.description: A distant view of the Minster at Ripon, from Studley Royal

paintings.title: Dunstanburgh Castle
paintings.description: A distant view of the iconic Northumbrian castle.

paintings.title: A Quiet Evening
paintings.description: A scene from Staveley Nature Reserve near Harrogate. The day had been stormy and unsettled but, as evening came on, the cloud began to break and a calmness settled over the lake and the willow trees.

paintings.title: Fields at Hambleton
paintings.description: Hambleton sits in the Vale of York, which offers expansive views. This image uses the verticals of tree and plant to break up the horizontals of the landscape.

paintings.title: Wheatfields at Hambleton
paintings.description: A view of the Vale of York with a series of striking trees to break up the flatness of the landscape

paintings.title: The Devil's Arrows
paintings.description: The Devil's Arrows are an impressive array of standing stones just outside of Boroughbridge. It is said the Devil hurled them at the town when the inhabitants displeased him!

paintings.title: Sunrise on Thruscross Moor
paintings.description: I was wandering the moor very early in the morning. The valley bottoms were shrouded in mist but on the moor, the rising sun provided a remarkable view

paintings.title: Country Lane at East Keswick
paintings.description: A rather grey day threw the tree formations into a greeny-black, contrasting with the winter greens of the fields.

paintings.title: Napes Hill - Leathley
paintings.description: A winter sunrise above the Napes Hill, overlooking Wharfedale

paintings.title: Sea Spray at Saltburn
paintings.description: This view of the Huntcliffe at Saltburn, is from the top of the beach at Marske, The day was windy and the distant cliffs were beginning to disappear in the resultant sea spray

paintings.title: Barden Tower
paintings.description: A summer's day in the Yorkshire Dales - Barden Tower shimmering in the afternoon sunlight

paintings.title: Hebden Ghyll - Misty Morning
paintings.description: Hebden Ghyll is a lovely stream winding through the landscape near Grassington in the Yorkshire Dales, carrying with it a certain air of mystery when wrapped in mist.

paintings.title: Gill House
paintings.description: Gill House sits at the top of Conistone Moor in the Yorkshire Dales. It was abandoned in the 1960s as it has no running water, gas, electricity or even a road! The ruins now shelter under the beautiful trees

paintings.title: Sycamore - Hebden Ghyll
paintings.description: This venerable tree can be found on the road above Hebden in the Yorkshire Dales. In winter one would think it is dead but as spring progresses it burgeons into life

paintings.title: High Garnshaw House
paintings.description: Morning light streams across Wharfedale as the overnight rain lifts

paintings.title: Early Spring Morning at Timble Ings
paintings.description: Very early morning on a beautiful spring day

paintings.title: Farnley Park - Early Autumn
paintings.description: The autumn of 2023 was a very gentle affair, lacking the high colours that are sometimes seen. But the soft shift from green to orange was quite beautiful, and none more so than on this magnificent oak tree that stands in the grounds of Farnley Hall.

paintings.title: Farnley Fields
paintings.description: An exercise in tonality from the fields near Farnley Park.

paintings.title: Home Farm, Farnley - from the Fields
paintings.description: Farnley Hall, near where I live, used to be the stomping ground of JMW Turner. He would spend most summers here, hunting and tramping around sketching. This scene looks back towards Home Farm, on the estate.

paintings.title: Dales View
paintings.description: Oil paint on board 30x21cm. A quick, expressive sketch looking towards the Dales.

paintings.title: Bamburgh Castle from the Wynd
paintings.description: A different view of Bamburgh Castle from the Wynd, an aptly named road that runs out to Stag Rocks

paintings.title: Lindisfarne Castle
paintings.description: The classic view of the iconic Northumbrian Castle

paintings.title: Nessend - Holy Island
paintings.description: Whilst most visitors to Holy Island congregate around the castle and harbour, the dunes on the the far side offer wonderful scenery and incredible wildlife.
